items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Brian has audio recording and video skills which he needs for his work. We are all working from home... It was fun. We did one episode... puts all our skills to use so it’s been a good thing to do together.

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m happy to have my guest Nicki Parrott here today, remotely unfortunately, but I did think it was worth gathering some stories for the Fillius Jazz Archive about how musicians and artists are making out these days. And we’ve seen some very upbeat examples of how you’re making out with your new online adventure and really enjoying Chez Nicki Jams.

Thank you. I’m so glad you are. I’ve had some really nice feedback from it because it feels like an escape but it’s also supporting a good cause, the World Central Kitchen, and they are needed right now. They are world-wide. They were helping in Australia when the bush fires were in Australia in January of this year and they’re helping out during the pandemic, you know, countless meals everyday, hoping to keep restaurants open to cook the meals for families. So that’s nice. It’s sort of — it started because we…
Yeah, I have one suggestion with episode four — you could have another subtitle, like how to use the electric bass in the kitchen. I wondered if that was —
